contexts.text: All the riches, all the labour, etc. = knowledges of faith.
Wealth and riches = the wealth and riches of wisdom and intelligence, thus knowledges.

All the wealth of Sodom and Gomorrah and all their food = evil and falsity; evil is here signified by wealth, and falsity by food. Spiritual wealth and riches, relatively to the good, are nothing but goods and truths with which they are endowed and enriched by the Lord. Thus wealth and riches, relatively to the evil, are nothing but evils and falsities that they have acquired for themselves. AC 1717.
Unless the Lord rendered aid...
In this combat man seems to press the Lord... to render aid...
The men put forth the hand = the Lord's powerful aid.
To carry their wealth upon the shoulder of young donkeys = knowledges that belong to their Rational.
The wealth of the nations = the immense abundance of natural good.
Such pass by those who most need aid.
I wait for Thy salvation Jehovah = unless the Lord renders aid. Explained.
When they who are in perception feel compassion they know that they are admonished by the Lord to render aid.
And Moses rose up and helped them = aid from the truths that belong to Law from the Divine.
And God heard their groaning = aid... To hear = to obey, but when it is said of the Lord, it = to provide and render aid, for he whom the Lord hears He renders aid to. AC 6852.
They who aspire to wealth not for the sake of wealth, but for the sake of the necessaries of life...
Because He hath heard your murmurings = on account of the suffering in temptation, that He may render aid.
Why tempt ye Jehovah? = that they are against the Divine, of whose aid they despaired.
And Jehovah said to Moses = aid.
Is Jehovah in the midst of us? = they almost believed that the Lord does not render aid to His own.
The reason why the Lord acts mediately through Heaven is not that He needs their aid, but that the Angels there may have functions and duties...
He who loves wealth above all things, whether money or possessions... NJHD 55.
If crying he shall cry unto Me = supplication to the Lord for aid. Explained.
Because I am merciful = that from Him is all aid, from mercy.
The most ancients... knew not what it was... to accumulate wealth beyond the necessaries of life.
Riches and wealth = those things that are of intelligence and wisdom, thus also knowledges of truth and of good, which are also called spiritual wealth and riches. Illustrated.
The love of the world is to will to draw to self by any arts whatever the wealth of others, and to set the heart on riches. NJHD 76.

But this love is manifold; there is the love of wealth for the sake of being advanced to honours... there is the love of honours and dignities in order to gain wealth, there is the love of wealth for the sake of various uses with which they are delighted in the world; there is the love of wealth merely for the sake of wealth... and so on. The end for the sake of which wealth is sought, is called the use, and it is the end or use from which the love has its quality. NJHD 77.
Subsidiary aid. See Subsidiary.

The Lord never draws a man away from seeking honours, and from procuring wealth; but He draws him away from the desire to seek honours for the sake of mere eminence... and from acquiring wealth for the sake of mere opulence, or for the sake of wealth...

Eternal things relate to spiritual honours and wealth, which are of love and wisdom, in Heaven. General article. The natural man... calls honours and wealth Divine blessings, and when he sees that the evil... are exalted to honours and promoted to wealth, he thinks... if the Divine Providence governed all things it would heap honours and wealth upon the good... He does not see that honours and wealth may be blessings and also may be curses... That honours and wealth are also given by the Devil...

Honours and wealth are blessings, and they are curses. General article. They are blessings with those who do not set their heart on them, and they are curses with those who do set their hearts on them. To set the heart on them, is to love them in themselves, and not to set the heart on them, is to love uses in them, and not themselves.
Dignities and wealth seduce some, and some they do not seduce: they seduce when they excite the loves of the man's proprium... but they do not seduce when they do not excite that love.
The evil... are exalted to honours and advanced to wealth, because the evil equally as the good do uses...

When dignities and wealth are blessings they are spiritual and eternal, and when they are curses they are temporary and perishable. General article. There are dignities and wealth in Heaven as in the world... for there are tradings there and thence wealth... dignities and wealth are themselves spiritual in the Spiritual Kingdom and celestial in the Celestial Kingdom, consequently those excel in dignities and wealth who excel in love and wisdom. These are they to whom dignities and wealth had been blessings in the world... Spiritual dignities and wealth are of the thing and not of the person.
That the dignities and wealth which are curses, compared with those which are blessings, are as nothing to everything, or as that which in itself is not to that which in itself is.

Riches and wealth are natural and temporary with those who have regard merely to them and to themselves in them... but the same are spiritual and eternal with those who have regard to good uses in them...
Those who are inwardly good and who outwardly like other men have laboured to gain wealth and have sought for honours...

A worshipper of self and of nature confirms himself against the Divine Providence when he sees the wicked... abounding in wealth... and worshippers of God in... poverty. General article... A worshipper of self and of nature believes dignities and wealth to be the greatest and only means of happiness... If in consequence of having been initiated into worship in his infancy, he thinks anything of God, he calls them Divine blessings... but in this worship there lies hidden what he himself is not aware of, that he may be advanced by God to still higher dignities and more abundant wealth, and if he attains thereto, his worship declines more and more to outward things, till it comes to nothing...

To the evil then, what are dignities and wealth but stumbling blocks? Not so to the good, because they do not set their hearts on them, but on the uses or goods for the doing of which dignities and wealth serve as means.
Man's life's love... has become of such a nature, that he wills to domineer over all, and to possess the whole wealth of the world.
Unless he acknowledges God and implores his aid...
Those who are in the visionary concupiscence or phantasy of possessing all wealth (visited and described).
The first affection of this age is the increasing of property by means of wealth...
There are three degrees of the natural man; in the first are they who love the world only, setting the heart on wealth; these are properly meant by the natural.
When the love of Heaven makes the head, it inflows into the love of the world, which is chiefly the love of wealth, and thereby performs uses. Explained.
No man of sound reason can condemn wealth, for it is in the general body as the blood is in man.
The wealth of all nations = knowledges wherever they are, even with the evil.
Wealth = spiritual wealth, which is knowledges of good and truth.
Works = knowledges of good, riches, knowledges of truth.
Riches = falsities. AE 538:10.
Wealth and riches = knowledges of truth.
Wealth and treasures = knowledges of truth and of good from the Word, but here, false scientific things, because from their own intelligence.
